properties.statement: [BL-192] Recording ONE change event took six rejected calls — every rejection individually correct, not one of them predictive
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Same field report, 2026-08-03, recording a container recreate against 3 nodes: a 3-minute bookkeeping task that cost ~8 round-trips.* In order: get_node{node_id} \u2192 *\"unknown field node_id, expected node_type or id\"* (the field is node_id in every RESPONSE and id in the request) \u00b7 set_verification_status{evidence} not a field \u00b7 record_change{affected_ids} not a field \u00b7 then *\"missing change_event_id\"*, revealing that record_change LINKS an existing event while add_change_event CREATES one \u2014 which neither its name nor its description said \u00b7 {affected: [\"cmp:embeddings\"]} \u2192 *\"expected struct AffectedNodeReq\"* without saying what that struct is \u00b7 {affected:[{node_type,id}]} \u2192 *\"unknown field id, expected node_type, node_id, action\"*, so the nested object wants node_id while the parent wants id, the exact inverse of get_node \u00b7 {change_type:\"modify\"} \u2192 *\"unknown change type\"* with no list of legal values. Only describe_schema ended it, returning ~8k tokens of edge documentation to answer *\"what are the 10 legal change_type values\"*. The cost lands exactly where it hurts most: at the moment the loop is most likely to be skipped under operational load \u2014 the failure PROTOCOL.md names as \"doing the bookkeeping without the loop\". Fixes, cheapest first: (1) enum rejections list the legal values \u2014 this alone kills three of the eight; (2) field-name rejections name the accepted spelling FOR THAT POSITION, the id/node_id inversion being the single biggest trap; (3) record_change's description says it links an existing ChangeEvent and points at add_change_event; (4) a describe_schema{properties_only:true} that returns the property table without the full edge catalogue. Size S", "origin": "Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-192 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: S."}
